bug_description.normalized: In `decode_NXAST_RAW_ENCAP`, Open vSwitch stores a local `encap` pointer into the heap-backed `ofpacts` buffer, then decodes attacker-controlled encap properties into the same buffer. On the saved witness input, `decode_ed_prop()` appends an NSH MDTYPE property and `ofpbuf_put_uninit()` grows `out` via `xrealloc()`, freeing the old 64-byte base. `decode_NXAST_RAW_ENCAP` does not reacquire `encap` after that reallocation and then writes `encap->n_props`, producing an AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2.

source.description: Reads the attacker-controlled `nx_action_encap` property slice into typed parser state by setting `ofp_prop = nae->props` and deriving `props_len` from `nae->len`. On the saved witness action this materializes one 8-byte property for the loop to decode.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` file is a single 72-byte OpenFlow 1.4 `PACKET_OUT` whose `actions_len` is 48; within the crashing encap action, `nae->len` is 24 so `props_len` becomes 8 and `ofp_prop` points at bytes `00 04 01 05 20 20 20 20`.

sink.description: Writes `n_props` through the stale `encap` pointer after the old `ofpacts` buffer has been freed by `xrealloc()`. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2 at this line.

root_cause.description: The function calls `decode_ed_prop(&ofp_prop, out, &props_len)` while keeping `encap` as a raw pointer into `out`, but it never refreshes that pointer after the property loop may grow `out`. The fix saves `encap`'s offset before the loop and reloads it with `ofpbuf_at_assert()` before the later writes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled encap action length is converted into `props_len`. For the saved witness, `nae->len = 24`, so `props_len = 8`, which drives exactly one property decode and the reallocating append.

coarse_trace.summary: After the OpenFlow message is admitted as `PACKET_OUT`, the printer allocates a 64-byte `ofpacts` buffer and enters packet-out decoding.
The OpenFlow 1.4 `PACKET_OUT` body contributes attacker-controlled `actions_len = 48`, and that action array is passed to the action decoder together with the heap-backed `ofpacts` buffer.
The crashing action is decoded as `RAW_ENCAP`; the function appends an internal `encap` object to `out` and materializes one 8-byte attacker-controlled property slice from the encap action.
The property bytes decode as an NSH MDTYPE property, and appending its internal form to `out` forces `ofpbuf_put_uninit()` to resize the 64-byte `ofpacts` allocation.
After the resize frees the old buffer, `decode_NXAST_RAW_ENCAP` still uses the stale `encap` pointer and crashes on `encap->n_props = n_props`.

fine_trace.note: After the witness message has been classified as `PACKET_OUT`, the printer allocates a 64-byte heap-backed `ofpacts` buffer to hold decoded internal actions. ASan's allocation stack shows this exact buffer originates from `ofpbuf_init()` via `xmalloc()`.

fine_trace.code: error = ofpacts_pull_openflow_actions(&b, ntohs(opo->actions_len), oh->version, NULL, NULL, ofpacts);
fine_trace.note: The PoC header byte `0x05` selects the OpenFlow 1.4 / `ofp11_packet_out` layout, and the attacker-controlled `actions_len` field is read as 48. Exactly those 48 action bytes from the 72-byte PoC are handed to the action decoder together with the heap buffer from step 1.

When the action decoder reaches the crashing encap action from the witness action array, it appends an internal `struct ofpact_encap` to `out` and stores the returned pointer in local variable `encap`. This alias points inside the same heap allocation created in step 1.

Consumes the attacker-controlled packet-type dispatch key from the current `nx_action_encap`. The witness action supplies one of the two supported values, so the function stays on the vulnerable path instead of returning `OFPERR_NXBAC_BAD_HEADER_TYPE`.

fine_trace.code: ofp_prop = nae->props; props_len = ntohs(nae->len) - offsetof(struct nx_action_encap, props);
fine_trace.note: Materializes the encap property's byte range from the attacker action. For the saved witness, `nae->len` is 24, so `props_len` becomes 8 and `ofp_prop` points to the single padded property bytes `00 04 01 05 20 20 20 20`.

Passes the live `out` buffer and the 8-byte attacker-controlled property slice into `decode_ed_prop()`. The local `encap` alias from step 3 stays live across this call even though appending a property may grow `out`; the function does not save an offset or reacquire `encap` before the later write.

The property header bytes decode as `prop_class = OFPPPC_NSH`, `prop_type = OFPPPT_PROP_NSH_MDTYPE`, and `len = 5`. They pass the local length checks and reach the append of the internal NSH-MDTYPE property object.

The append from step 7 needs more tailroom than remains in the 64-byte `ofpacts` buffer on this witness, so `ofpbuf_put_uninit()` grows `out` and `xrealloc()` frees the old base. ASan records the freed allocation as the 64-byte region `[0x6060000001a0, 0x6060000001e0)`. `b->data` and `b->header` are updated to the new base, but local `encap` in `decode_NXAST_RAW_ENCAP` still points into the freed old base.

After `decode_ed_prop()` returns successfully, the function counts the decoded property. On the witness path `n_props` becomes 1 and `props_len` is exhausted, so the loop is about to leave the property block with `encap` still stale because no reload from `out` has happened.

Writes the 16-bit value `1` through the stale `encap` pointer into the freed old `ofpacts` allocation. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 2 at `0x6060000001da`, 58 bytes inside the freed 64-byte region.

poc.trigger: The saved 72-byte PoC drives `ofputil_decode_packet_out()` into `decode_NXAST_RAW_ENCAP()`, where decoding the encap property list forces `ofpacts` to be reallocated and the subsequent `encap->n_props = n_props` write hits the stale pre-reallocation pointer.

format.name: OpenFlow 1.4 PACKET_OUT
format.contract: Exact 72-byte witness stored at `poc`: one OpenFlow 1.4 (`version = 0x05`) `PACKET_OUT` (`type = 0x0d`, `length = 0x0048`) with `actions_len = 48`; within the crashing encap action, `nae->len = 24`, so the decoder sees exactly one 8-byte property slice `00 04 01 05 20 20 20 20`, which is sufficient on the witnessed path to reach the reallocating property append and then the stale `encap->n_props` write.
